---
title: "Random-effect distributions"
---

> **Maturity: experimental** — see [Feature Maturity](../maturity.qmd) for what this means.

By default every ETA is Gaussian, `η ~ N(0, Ω)`. A `density` clause on its
`omega` line gives it another distribution instead
([#1716](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1716)):

```
[parameters]
  theta TVCL(4.0, 0.1, 100.0)
  theta TVV(30.0, 1.0, 500.0)
  theta TVF(0.6, 0.01, 0.99)
  theta NU(10.0, 2.5, 100.0)
  omega ETA_CL ~ 0.09 density gamma
  omega ETA_F  ~ 0.02 density beta(TVF)
  omega ETA_V  ~ 0.06 density t(NU)

[individual_parameters]
  CL = TVCL * ETA_CL      # Gamma-distributed clearance, mean TVCL
  F  = ETA_F              # Beta-distributed bioavailability, mean TVF
  V  = TVV * exp(ETA_V)   # heavy-tailed log volume
```

As in Pumas's `@random` block, the ETA *is* the distributed quantity: under
`density gamma`, `ETA_CL` is a positive random variable with mean 1, so
`CL = TVCL * ETA_CL` has mean `TVCL` exactly. There is none of the mean bias of
`TVCL * exp(η)` or of a logit-normal fraction.

### What to write in `[individual_parameters]`

The read depends on where the kind lives, because the ETA already is the effect
on its support:

| Kind's support | Proportional (log scale) | Additive |
|---|---|---|
| ℝ (no `density`, or `t`, `logistic`, …) | `CL = TVCL * exp(ETA_CL)` | `CL = TVCL + ETA_CL` |
| (0, ∞) (`gamma`, `lognormal`, …) | `CL = TVCL * ETA_CL` | not meaningful: it shifts TVCL by the kind's mean or median of 1 |
| (0, 1) (`beta`, `logitnormal`) | `F = ETA_F` | — |

An additive Gaussian ETA needs no clause. A positive or (0, 1) ETA read inside
`exp`, `log`, `inv_logit` or `logit` is refused, with the line to write: under
`density gamma`, `TVCL * exp(ETA_CL)` would fit `TVCL·exp(Gamma)`, which is
rarely what was meant when a `density` was added to an existing line. A
positive ETA added to a term (`TVCL + ETA_CL`) is valid but almost never meant,
so it is the warning `W_DENSITY_ADDITIVE`.

## Distributions

Every distribution Pumas's `@random` block takes for a scalar or vector random
effect is available. The name after `density` is Pumas's, lower-cased; the
aliases in parentheses also work. The value on the `omega` line is ω.

`(sd)` squares the number written into ω, and reads the same on either side of
the clause: `omega ETA_CL ~ 0.3 (sd) density gamma` and
`omega ETA_CL ~ 0.3 density gamma (sd)` both declare ω = 0.09. For a kind whose
ω is a variance, `(sd)` is the effect's SD; for `t` and `cauchy`, whose ω is the
scale², it is the scale. `levy` takes its scale as ω itself, so `(sd)` is
refused there.

### On ℝ

| `density` | parameterisation | shape θ |
|---|---|---|
| `t(ν)` (`studentt`) | scale² ω; a `block_omega` is multivariate t | ν > 0 |
| `logistic` | mean 0, variance ω | — |
| `laplace` | mean 0, variance ω | — |
| `cauchy` | scale² ω | — |
| `gumbel` | mean 0, variance ω | — |
| `nig(ζ, ρ)` (`normalinversegaussian`) | mean 0, variance ω; ζ tail, ρ skew | ζ > 0, −1 < ρ < 1 |
| `pgeneralizedgaussian(p)` (`pgg`) | mean 0, variance ω | p > 0 |
| `gev(ξ)` (`generalizedextremevalue`) | mean 0, variance ω | ξ < ½ |
| `arcsine`, `uniform` | mean 0, variance ω, on a symmetric interval | — |
| `biweight`, `triweight`, `epanechnikov`, `cosine`, `semicircle`, `symtriangular` | mean 0, variance ω, on a symmetric interval | — |

### On (0, ∞)

| `density` | parameterisation | shape θ |
|---|---|---|
| `gamma`, `chisq` | mean 1, variance ω (a scaled χ² is a gamma) | — |
| `invgamma` (`inversegamma`) | mean 1, variance ω | — |
| `lognormal` | median 1, `ln η ~ N(0, ω)`: exactly the classic `TV·exp(η)` | — |
| `lognormal_mean` | mean 1, variance ω (`ln η ~ N(−s²/2, s²)`, `s² = ln(1 + ω)`) | — |
| `chi` | mean 1, variance ω (a scaled χ, i.e. Nakagami) | — |
| `weibull`, `frechet` | mean 1, variance ω (shape solved from ω) | — |
| `inversegaussian` | mean 1, variance ω | — |
| `betaprime` | mean 1, variance ω | — |
| `noncentralchisq(k)` | mean 1, variance ω | k > 0 |
| `pareto`, `gpd` (`generalizedpareto`) | mean 1, variance ω | — |
| `levy` | scale ω (no mean) | — |
| `exponential`, `rayleigh`, `kolmogorov` | fixed shape (mean 1; Kolmogorov unscaled) | — |
| `erlang(k)` | mean 1, variance 1/k | k > 0 |
| `loguniform(a, b)` | on (a, b) | 0 < a < b |

`exponential`, `rayleigh`, `erlang`, `kolmogorov` and `loguniform` have no free
spread, so their omega is unused and must be declared `FIX`.

### On (0, 1)

| `density` | parameterisation | shape θ |
|---|---|---|
| `beta(μ)` | mean μ, variance ω (needs ω < μ(1 − μ)) | μ in [0, 1] |
| `logitnormal(μ)` | `logit η ~ N(logit μ, ω)` | μ in [0, 1] |

### Truncation and the rest of Pumas's list

`density truncated(KIND, LO, HI)` restricts any univariate kind to `(LO, HI)`,
renormalised: `truncated(gamma, 0.2, 5)`, `truncated(t(NU), -1, inf)`. A bound is
a number, `inf` / `-inf`, or a `FIX`ed θ. The random effect is read through a
bounded map, so the latent stays unconstrained. Pumas's `Constrained` is the same
thing, and its `product_distribution` is one `omega` line per ETA. `normalcanon`
and `normal` are the default Gaussian.

Wishart, InverseWishart, LKJ and LKJCholesky are distributions of a matrix. A
ferx ETA is a scalar, or a vector under `block_omega`, so they are not random-
effect distributions here; they are priors on Ω.

A shape θ is named inside the parentheses, or declared automatically by empty
ones: `density t()` declares `NU_ETA_V`, `density beta()` declares `MU_ETA_F`.

### Blocks and copulas

Three distributions take a `block_omega`:

- `density t(ν)` is a multivariate t with one ν and scale matrix Ω.
- `density lognormal` is Pumas's `MvLogNormal` with `ln η ~ N(0, Ω)`, the
  classic correlated `TV·exp(η)` block; `density lognormal_mean` gives each
  effect mean 1, with Ω their covariance.
- `density copula(ETA = KIND, …)` gives each ETA its own univariate margin,
  joined by a Gaussian copula. Ω's diagonal holds each margin's ω, and its
  off-diagonal holds the correlations of the margins' normal scores:

```
  block_omega (ETA_CL, ETA_F) = [0.09, 0.01, 0.02] density copula(ETA_CL = gamma, ETA_F = beta(TVF))
```

A copula of `normal` margins is the multivariate normal. Every other kind is
univariate, and a block of it is refused.

### IOV kappas

A `kappa` line takes the same clause: `kappa K_CL ~ 0.04 density t(NU)`. One
distribution is shared by every occasion's κ, and the occasions stay
independent. A `block_kappa` takes the block forms above. A density on a κ that
spans two nested levels is refused with `E_DENSITY_UNSUPPORTED`.

### FREM and mixtures

FREM joins each covariate ETA to the parameter ETAs. When a parameter ETA
carries a univariate density, the joined block becomes a copula. The covariate
ETAs keep `normal` margins, so the covariate model is unchanged.

A `[mixture]` class that overrides a density ETA's omega gives that class its
own ω. The class's density M-step moves it, as it does the shared ω. Under SAEM,
a class's subjects leave the shared step of that ETA's group only; every other
density group still steps on them.

### Multimodal effects

Every kind here is unimodal: the transforms are monotone maps of a Gaussian η,
and the kinds are single-peaked (`arcsine` is U-shaped, but it is a bounded
effect, not two subpopulations). For a bimodal clearance, use a
[`[mixture]`](../estimation/mixture.qmd): it gives each class its own typical
value and ω, an estimated mixing probability, and each subject's class
probability, as NONMEM's `$MIXTURE` does. It composes with a density, so each
class can have a Gamma-shaped spread around its own typical value:

```
[parameters]
  theta TVCL1(2.0, 0.1, 100.0)
  theta TVCL2(8.0, 0.1, 100.0)
  theta MIXL(0.4, -5.0, 5.0)
  omega ETA_CL ~ 0.09 density gamma

[individual_parameters]
  CL = if (MIXNUM == 1) TVCL1 * ETA_CL else TVCL2 * ETA_CL

[mixture]
  nsub = 2
  logit(1) = MIXL
  omega(2) ETA_CL ~ 0.04
```

## Transforms

The other way to get a non-Gaussian random effect keeps η ~ N(0, ω) and has the
model read a transform `h(η)`. That is declared in the
[`[eta_shape]` block](eta-shape.qmd), not on the `omega` line:

```
[eta_shape]
  ETA_CL ~ boxcox(LAMBDA)
```

`[eta_shape]` is the one declarative home for a transform. An omega-line
`transform KIND(…)` and `density boxcox(λ)` are refused with the `[eta_shape]`
line to write instead. On its latent scale a Box-Cox density *is* the Box-Cox
transform, so `density boxcox` would only have been a second spelling of the
same model.

## How it is estimated

The estimators work on an unconstrained **latent** `z` for each density ETA,
and the model reads the random effect `m(z)`. The map is the identity on ℝ,
`exp` on (0, ∞) and `inv_logit` on (0, 1). The parser applies it to every read
of the ETA in `[individual_parameters]`. The prior is the exact latent density
`p_z(z) = p_η(m(z))·|m′(z)|`. So a constrained effect never leaves its support,
and the Laplace and FOCE machinery runs where the posterior is smooth.

Pumas maps a constrained random effect the same way. See
[Reporting](#reporting) for which scale each output reports.

The prior's value, gradient and Hessian are exact, from dual numbers over one
implementation, and the likelihood kernel's compiled plans record that same
implementation, so the FOCEI and Laplace adjoint gradients are exact too,
including `∂/∂ω` and `∂/∂ν` / `∂/∂μ`. No density kind falls back to finite
differences: a special function (the Bessel `K₁` of the NIG, the normal quantile
of a copula, the incomplete gamma and beta of a truncation's mass) is one
recorded primitive, and a shape solved from ω (Weibull, Fréchet, chi) is the
root refined by Newton steps, whose derivatives are those of the exact root.
The per-kind check against reconverged finite differences of the objective is in
`every_smooth_density_kind_matches_reconverged_fd_through_the_plans`.

- **FOCEI / Laplace / AGQ**: the conditional objective, with the density's
  curvature in `H̃`.
- **FOCE** (no interaction): the Sheiner–Beal marginal integrates η as a
  Gaussian, so a density model takes the conditional form FOCE uses beside a
  non-Gaussian endpoint (variance at the EBE, no interaction term; on a
  correlated residual, the dense form without it). On a Gaussian model it is
  unchanged.
- **IMP / IMPMAP**: importance weights use the exact prior; the Gaussian
  defensive proposal stays a proposal.
- **SAEM / MCEM**: a density group's ω and shape θ have no sufficient
  statistic, so they move by Fisher scoring on their exact score, one step per
  SAEM iteration (NONMEM's rule for such parameters) and to convergence per
  MCEM iteration. Gaussian ETAs keep their closed form.
- **Bayes**: the η and θ moves score the exact prior (so the shape θs are
  sampled against it). A density group's Ω block has no conjugate update, so it
  moves by a Metropolis step on its log-Cholesky factor, under the marginal the
  Ω prior puts on that block (an inverse gamma for one ETA under the default).
  `bayes_omega_prior` in `[fit_options]` picks the Ω prior:
  `inversewishart` (the default, conjugate for Gaussian blocks), `wishart`, or
  `lkj(η)` (an LKJ(η) prior on the correlations, with an inverse-gamma prior on
  each variance). Under the last
  two, every block moves by the Metropolis step.
- **VI**: the KL term is sampled with the exact prior, and after each iteration
  a density group's ω and shape θ maximise the prior half of the ELBO over the
  variational draws (the MCEM objective).
- **Simulation** draws each kind from its own distribution.

A density ETA is not mu-referenced, with one exception: `density lognormal`
(median 1, untruncated) *is* the Gaussian `TV·exp(η)`, so it is compiled as
that Gaussian ETA, mu-referencing and every closed form included, and reports
`lognormal` as its distribution.

## Reporting

**Typical values.** Every θ row that is an individual parameter's typical value
says which summary of the parameter it is:

```
  TVCL             4.310000     0.210000     4.87  (mean of CL)
  TVV             32.100000     1.400000     4.36  (median of V)
```

`TV·exp(η)` with a symmetric η (Gaussian, a shape transform, `t`, `logistic`,
`lognormal`) makes TV the **median**, and `TV + η` the **mean**. A positive
density whose effect has mean 1 (`gamma`, `lognormal_mean`, …) read as `TV·η`
makes TV the **mean**. An asymmetric kind on ℝ under `exp` (`gumbel`, `gev`,
`nig`) makes it the **geometric mean**, `exp(E[ln P])`. The μ of `beta(μ)` is the
mean of the parameter, and that of `logitnormal(μ)` the median. A θ shared by
two parameters gets no label. The fit YAML carries the same as
`typical_value_of` and `typical_value_statistic` on the θ entry
(`FitResult::typical_values`).

**Omega rows.** A CV% or SD on ω does not describe a non-Gaussian effect the way
it describes a Gaussian one, and some kinds (Cauchy, Lévy, t with ν ≤ 2) have no
SD at all. So a density ETA's omega row is followed by a line with its
distribution, what ω is where it is not the effect's variance, its exact mean
with the CV% (or the SD when the mean is 0) where both moments exist in closed
form, the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of the effect the model reads at the
estimates, and, when the covariance step ran, a 95% interval for each
percentile:

```
  ETA_CL               = 0.030083  SE = 0.008120
                         density gamma (mean 1, CV% = 17.3): 5/50/95% = 0.7328 / 0.9900 / 1.3013; 95% CI [0.6703, 0.8011] / [0.9871, 0.9926] / [1.2196, 1.3804]
  ETA_V                = 0.010632  SE = 0.003310
                         density t(NU), ω = scale² (mean 0, SD = 0.1145): 5/50/95% = -0.1858 / 0.0000 / 0.1858; …
```

The percentiles come from inverting the exact CDF, not from sampling. Their
intervals are the 2.5% and 97.5% points of the same percentiles over 500 draws
of the parameters from the covariance step's matrix (the asymptotic draws
`simulate_with_uncertainty` uses), with a fixed seed. A κ with a density gets
the same line under its KAPPA row. The fit YAML carries it per omega entry:
`distribution`, `distribution_form`, `distribution_shapes`, `truncation`,
`effect_quantiles_5_50_95`, `effect_quantiles_ci_95`, `effect_mean`,
`effect_sd` and `effect_cv_pct`. A truncation bound that is a θ is read at its
estimate.

::: {.callout-important}
## Mean or median

`density lognormal` is the classic `TVCL * exp(η)`: `TVCL` is the **median**,
ω the variance of `log CL`, and the CV is `√(exp(ω) − 1)`.
`density lognormal_mean` pins the effect's **mean** at 1 instead, so
`CL = TVCL * ETA_CL` has mean `TVCL`, ω is the variance of the effect itself,
and the CV is exactly `√ω`. The two ωs are not interchangeable.
:::

**Which scale each output reports.** Every output reports a density ETA's EBE
on the scale of the effect the model reads, `m(ẑ)` (`exp(ẑ)` for a gamma), so
`TVCL * ETA_CL` evaluated at the reported EBE is the subject's CL:
`ferx_core::io::output::eta_effects` (`fit$ebe_etas` in R), the conditional
distribution file's `COND_MEAN`, `COND_SD` and `COND_MODE`, and the values
`SuppliedEtas` takes for `predict` / `simulate` (a value outside the kind's
support is refused). `SubjectResult::eta` keeps the latent `ẑ`, the coordinates
the estimators work in, so a `.fitrx` reload continues exactly; in R it is
`fit$ebe_latent`. A Gaussian ETA reads the same on both.

A density ETA's **shrinkage** is computed on the effect: `1 − RMS(m(ẑ) − μ)/σ`,
with the kind's exact prior mean μ and SD σ. The Gaussian formula
`1 − RMS(ẑ)/√ω` would compare the latent with the effect's variance and assume a
centred latent. Where those moments have no closed form (a truncation, a t with
ν ≤ 2, Cauchy, Lévy) it is the quantile analogue `1 − IQR(m(ẑ))/IQR(prior)`,
which equals the first for a Gaussian spread of EBEs.

In code, `FitResult::eta_param_info[..].distribution`,
`FitResult::kappa_distributions`, `FitResult::typical_values` and
`FitResult::eta_effect_quantile_ci` hold the metadata, and
`ferx_core::io::output::{eta_distribution_note, kappa_distribution_note,
eta_effect_quantiles, eta_effects}` give the rest.

## Limits

Seven kinds have a kink or a hard edge where their density is still positive:
`laplace` and `symtriangular` (the peak), `uniform`, `arcsine`, `loguniform`
and `pareto` (the edges), and `gpd` (its upper edge for ω < 1). A method whose
reported objective reads the prior's curvature at the EBE gets a curvature that
does not exist at a kink and cannot see an edge. So these kinds are
**refused** with `E_DENSITY_UNSUPPORTED`, naming the ETA, under FOCE, FOCEI, the
Gauss–Newton pair, Laplace, VI's `vi_final_ofv = laplace` and SAEM's
`saem_ofv = focei`. They run under:

- **IMP / IMPMAP**: `ofv`, AIC and BIC are the importance-sampling `−2 log L`
  (`ofv_type: importance_sampling` in the YAML), not the final Laplace pass an
  IMP fit otherwise reports. If the marginal cannot be evaluated, `ofv` is NaN
  with `W_DENSITY_NO_OBJECTIVE`, rather than a Laplace value.
- **SAEM** under `saem_ofv = saem`, `imp` or `agq`: these score the prior
  itself. The FOCE/Laplace value SAEM otherwise shows as a diagnostic is
  omitted.
- **Bayes**, whose posterior intervals need no curvature.

The covariance step (and SIR, whose proposal is that step's matrix)
differentiates the FOCE/Laplace objective, so it is skipped for these kinds
with `W_DENSITY_NO_COVARIANCE`; fit with `method = bayes` for intervals.

## Validation

NONMEM has no non-Gaussian random-effect prior, so its anchors are reductions
to a model it can run, and Stan anchors the rest. The checks are:

- **NONMEM reductions.** `density lognormal_mean` is an affine map of a Gaussian
  η, so its FOCEI objective is that of NONMEM's Gaussian stream: OFV within
  6.4e-8, EBEs within 2.4e-8 (`the_lognormal_density_matches_nonmem`).
  `density logistic` as `F⁻¹(Φ(η))` under IMP is compared net of a Gaussian IMP
  null, within 1.9e-5.
- **Stan.** The `method = bayes` posterior of a Gamma clearance on warfarin
  matches Stan's (`tests/eta_density_stan_anchor.rs`).

- **Closed forms and quadrature.** Each latent density integrates to 1, the
  random effect has the documented mean and variance (quadrature to 3e-14), the
  bivariate t matches the textbook log-density, and the gradients and Hessians
  match their hand-derived closed forms.
- **Reduction to an anchored model.** A `logitnormal(μ)` density is a Gaussian
  translated by `logit μ`, so its FOCEI objective and adjoint gradient equal the
  Gaussian model `inv_logit(logit(MU) + ETA)`, to 1e-15.
- **One objective.** The adjoint kernel's objective is the production
  objective exactly, and its inner gradient vanishes at production's EBE.
